headline: High: Aider’s shared-git, shell, and broad egress can conflict with dbt-core’s warehouse writes and create default-path data and compliance risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read and write repo files and uses shared git state, so malicious content in files could be copied into prompts or edits. dbt-core mainly consumes warehouse/project inputs and has allowlisted egress, but no direct instruction channel is documented. The bridge is plausible through files, not proven by evidence.
conditions: IF Aider is pointed at a repository containing attacker-controlled prompt text or instructions, it may ingest them.
IF dbt-core outputs are copied into Aider-managed files without review, those instructions can influence later edits.
mitigations: Review repo files for instruction-like text before opening them in Aider.
Keep prompt-bearing notes outside the shared repo.
Use separate branches for generated artifacts and human-authored prompts.
Add a short manual review step before Aider applies edits.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and can send context to configured model providers; dbt-core touches warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress. In a shared workspace, sensitive warehouse outputs can flow into Aider prompts or commits, creating a default-path leakage risk even without a documented direct bridge.
conditions: IF dbt-core materializes sensitive warehouse rows into files in the shared repo, Aider can read them.
IF Aider is configured with a third-party model provider, file contents may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Keep warehouse extracts out of the shared repo.
Redact secrets and PII before Aider sees generated files.
Use a separate workspace for dbt artifacts and code edits.
Restrict Aider to non-sensitive branches when possible.
Verify model-provider logging settings before running either agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git-state modification in a shared repo; dbt-core can also mutate warehouse state through API calls. That overlap creates a real write/write conflict surface, and the shared git repo plus lack of locking makes concurrent edits and state drift dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository concurrently, commits and file edits can race.
IF dbt-core writes to shared warehouse objects while Aider edits generated SQL, the two can diverge without coordination.
mitigations: Serialize runs on the shared repo.
Use separate branches per agent.
Add a lock file or orchestrator mutex before edits.
Pause dbt runs while Aider is rewriting SQL models.
Review git diffs before merging either agent’s changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate or rewrite code and dbt-core can execute warehouse transformations, so Aider’s output may become dbt-core input with no built-in verification step. dbt-core is not documented here as critically evaluating upstream text, so a mistaken edit can cascade into incorrect transformations or broken models.
conditions: IF Aider edits dbt models or SQL that dbt-core later executes, errors can propagate downstream.
IF dbt-core is run immediately after Aider without review, incorrect assumptions can become warehouse actions.
mitigations: Require a human diff review before dbt runs.
Run dbt tests after any Aider-generated change.
Limit Aider to non-executable documentation files when possible.
Use CI checks to block unreviewed model changes.
Keep a rollback plan for failed warehouse runs.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history locally, while dbt-core touches warehouse data and can move regulated data into analytics workflows. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or certification alignment, so the safest reading is a compliance mismatch risk on shared data classes rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and is surfaced into the shared repo, retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF either agent logs outputs to a third-party service, policy obligations may change.
mitigations: Classify warehouse extracts before sharing them with Aider.
Confirm retention settings for both the repo and warehouse.
Avoid placing regulated data in git-tracked files.
Check whether any third-party model provider is in scope for compliance.
Document a deletion/export process for generated artifacts.
